prompt_text: I need a personal injury attorney in Chicago after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
Below are several reputable Chicago personal-injury law firms you should consider calling after a car accident, plus why each might be a good fit. I also include quick next steps, what to ask at the free consultation, and what documents to bring.

Specific firms to call (and why)
- Clifford Law Offices — A large, well-known Chicago plaintiffs’ firm with extensive experience handling serious car-crash, catastrophic-injury, and wrongful-death cases. Good if you expect a complex case or large damages and need a firm with trial resources.
- Corboy & Demetrio — Long-established trial firm in Chicago focused on personal injury and wrongful death. Known for aggressive representation and trial experience in high-stakes auto cases.
- Levin & Perconti — A Chicago plaintiffs’ firm with a reputation for medical malpractice and personal-injury cases, including serious auto collisions; they handle catastrophic injuries and have experience with insurance negotiations and trials.
- Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard, P.C. — Plaintiffs’ personal injury firm that regularly handles auto-accident and severe-injury claims; often cited for client service and personal attention.
- Power Rogers & Smith — Plaintiff personal injury attorneys in Chicago who handle car crashes and truck accidents and emphasize client communication and trial readiness.
- (Alternative) Large national firms with local Chicago presence — If you prefer a bigger national firm’s resources, consider checking national plaintiff firms that have Chicago offices (many offer free consultations and contingency-fee arrangements).

Why these kinds of firms
- Trial experience: If the insurer does not offer a fair settlement, you want lawyers who will and can take the case to trial.
- Resources: Big or well-established plaintiffs’ firms can handle medical liens, expert witnesses, and expensive litigation costs up front.
- Local knowledge: Firms based in Chicago will know Cook County judges, local hospital networks, and insurers active in the area.
- Contingency work: Most personal-injury lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Confirm the percentage and who pays costs.

Other ways to find and vet attorneys
- Chicago Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service or Illinois Trial Lawyers Association (ITLA) — both can provide vetted referrals.
- Check recent client reviews, peer ratings (Martindale-Hubbell), and whether the firm limits itself to plaintiff-side work.
- Call 3 firms and compare: responsiveness, whether an attorney (not just a paralegal) handles your consult, and how they would approach your case.

What to ask at the free consultation
- Do you handle car-accident cases? What percentage of your practice is auto/personal injury?
- Do you take cases on contingency? What is your fee and what costs are deducted?
- Will a trial attorney handle my case or is it passed to a junior lawyer?
- Do you have experience with cases like mine (neck/back injury, TBI, spinal injury, wrongful death, uninsured motorist)?
- How long do you expect this to take and what is a realistic value range?
- Will you handle medical liens and coordinate with health providers?
- Can you provide recent client references or results (general examples)?

What to bring to the consultation (or have ready)
- Police report number / copy of the accident report
- Photos of the scene, vehicles, and injuries
- Insurance information for all drivers involved
- Medical records and bills related to the accident (or dates/places of treatment)
- Repair estimates or photos of vehicle damage
- Any correspondence with insurers (release forms, settlement offers)
- Names and contact info for witnesses

Timing and legal deadlines
- Illinois’ statute of limitations for personal injury is generally 2 years from the date of the accident (there are exceptions). If a government entity is involved, notice deadlines can be much shorter. Call a lawyer promptly to preserve your rights and evidence.

Practical tips now
- Get prompt medical care and follow treatment recommendations.
- Preserve evidence: photos, witness names, damaged property.
- Avoid giving recorded statements to insurers before speaking to a lawyer.
- Document time off work and out-of-pocket expenses.

If you’d like, tell me:
- the date and basic facts of the crash,
- the injuries you sustained, and
- whether the other driver was insured,

and I can (a) suggest which of the firms above might be the best match for your situation, or (b) draft a short script/email you can use when contacting them.
